title: window.ml execution log export
description: One run's mechanics as a FILE, which is what the panel's download writes. A bare array was the obvious thing and is the wrong one: it carries no version, nothing saying which run it is of, and nothing saying when it was taken — all three of which a file read six months later needs and a panel does not. Normative shape, published as `docs/spec/run-log.schema.json` (generated from here; see scripts/gen-export-schema.mjs).

run.description: The run it is of — absent when the whole ring was exported rather than one run's records.

RunLogEvent.description: One thing the machinery did on a run's behalf. A housekeeping event plus WHOSE run it was, since the whole point is reading one run's mechanics beside its steps. `subsystem` and `kind` are open by intent, exactly as they are there: a new mechanism adds its own rather than extending an enum every consumer generated from.

reason.description: Why: `"budget"`, `"idle"`, `"timeout"`, `"session-end"`, … — what tells a budget eviction from an idle one.

key.description: What it acted on: a URL, a pointer id, a session hash. Withheld from a page reading events it did not report.

tab.description: The reporting tab, for `origin: "page"` — how a page's own events are told from another tab's.

detail.description: Anything else, small and flat. Withheld from a page reading events it did not report.

run.description: The run's id, which is its session hash (`runId: runHash`, ml-agent-run.ts).
